script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 20. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

For 165 million years, they ruled.  From tiny feathered creatures to 100-foot giants, dinosaurs dominated every continent.  Then, in geological instant, they were gone—except for one lineage that still soars overhead.

Dinosaurs appeared about 230 million years ago and dominated until 66 million years ago. That's 165 million years of rule. Humans have existed for about 300,000 years. If dinosaur history were a 24-hour day, human history would be less than 3 minutes. Not all dinosaurs died.  One lineage—small, feathered theropods—survived and evolved into birds.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: 165 million years of dominance ended in a cosmic instant.  Nothing—no matter how powerful—lasts forever.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Deep Time Perspective - See the Long View.

Here's your activity: Consider something that feels permanent in your life—a job, a relationship, an institution. Now imagine it from a 'dinosaur perspective': millions of years from now, what trace will it leave? How does this perspective change how you hold it? This helps you develop perspective through geological time scales.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about when dinosaurs ruled can be applied to deep time perspective - see the long view. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
